_comment: IAW status/bitfield decoders. 'enum' = value maps to one label; 'bits' = value is a bitmask, list every set flag. 'base' = radix of the keys. Attach to a param in params.json via {"map":"<name>","map_type":"enum|bits"} once the status-carrying rli is identified; the raw value is still logged.

motorstate._note: 0x58 read against 0x30/0x34/0x33 on 2026-09-05 (326 samples): only 0, 5, 6 and 7 ever appeared. 0x04 stands for as long as the engine turns and is the only bit left when it stops. 0x01 follows the throttle a sample ahead of 0x34 -- set while it sits at 1.7-2.0 deg, clear the moment it opens past 4.8 -- so it is the closed-throttle/idle condition, not a power state. 0x02 came up once as the coolant crossed 53->54 C and never cleared again, which reads as the after-start/warm-up phase ending. The three high bits were never observed here, so their meaning is still a guess and they are labelled as such. The old labels (0x01 'Power-On, engine OFF', 0x02 'Ignition ON, engine OFF') contradicted the data -- they were set with the engine running.

clutch._note: polarity verified on the bike 2026-09-04: the ECU answers 0 while the lever is pulled (the engine was started that way) and 1 with it released -- the reference table had it the other way round

lambda_loop._note: 0x49 on the 2026-09-04 warm-up: a flat 0 for the first 43 s from cold, then 0<->2 at the rate the sensor itself switches -- 2 is the closed-loop correction being applied
